raised.quote:
if (!allowedKeys.has(verdict.new_issue_key!)) { skipped++; continue; }
      pushInto(byKey, verdict.new_issue_key!, verdict);
raised.claim: The scope guard checks attachments to existing issues but not the initial attachments to a new issue.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a proposal is scoped to `candidates_count > 0` and a zero-candidate row references its key, the planner still creates the issue with that verdict and the job writes the issue link. The same row would be rejected if sent to the same issue on the next run.

raised.claim: Model-written issue prose can supply the first scope block and override the structured scope on the next run.
raised.why_it_breaks: When the free-form body includes an illustrative `triage-scope` block, the job puts it before the authoritative block and the parser takes the first match. A valid example silently changes routing; a malformed example makes the issue unscoped even though a valid block follows.

raised.claim: The saturation guard does not count attachments already accepted for the same issue in the current batch.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue with 11 post-creation rows and five qualifying verdicts passes the same check five times. The job posts all five, bringing the issue to 16 despite the configured maximum of 12.

raised.claim: An empty result from either probe satisfies the absence gate even when the other probe returned the beer.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a brewery-only query misses a misspelled brewery but the name-only query returns the exact beer under the correct brewery, a mistaken `not_on_untappd` verdict still passes. The stored class then blocks the metered web fallback despite the positive evidence.

raised.claim: Guard counts are only logged when the model omits an in-batch verdict, not when the guards refuse or downgrade verdicts.
raised.why_it_breaks: If the model returns a verdict for every row and all of them contradict their target scopes, `covered` still equals the batch size. No warning carries `scope_violation`, so the repeated rejection loop this log is meant to diagnose remains unexplained.

raised.claim: The new absence fallback sends rows into a reporting path that counts quiet `matcher_bug` verdicts as `wontfix`.
raised.why_it_breaks: A run with three unprobed absence verdicts persists three `matcher_bug` reviews, but the job increments `outcome.wontfix` for each because its quiet loop treats every non-`not_on_untappd` verdict as `wontfix`. The digest reports three intentional exclusions although none occurred.

raised.quote:
if (scope.beer_ids.length > 0) return true;
  return scope.where.some((t) => t.col !== 'review_class');
raised.claim: The legality check allows whole-class scopes when a cohort is also present or when the non-class condition is a tautology.
raised.why_it_breaks: A scope with one enumerated ID and a `where` consisting only of `review_class = matcher_bug` passes, and the OR semantics admit every other `matcher_bug` row. Without IDs, adding `candidates_count >= 0` has the same effect for ordinary failure rows.

raised.quote:
const parsed = ScopeSchema.safeParse(JSON.parse(m[1]));
    return parsed.success ? parsed.data : null;
raised.claim: Read-back validates scope shape but does not enforce the legality rule on existing issues.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a backfill or manual edit adds a structured block with no beer IDs and only `review_class = matcher_bug`, the parser accepts it and the existing-issue guard allows any matching verdict below the cap. The same block on a new proposal would be rejected.

raised.claim: Enumerated scope exceptions are trusted even if the named IDs were not actually attached when the issue was created.
raised.why_it_breaks: A proposal can list an older beer ID copied from issue context, or a current-batch ID whose attachment was discarded, in addition to a valid creation verdict. If that beer later enters triage, its stale inclusion lets it attach even when it contradicts the issue's column predicates.

raised.claim: The new authoritative issue link survives the review reset that clears the class, note, and review timestamp.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a reviewed beer linked to #408 changes from zero candidates to nonzero candidates, `recordEnrichFailure` reopens it for triage without clearing `issue_number`. A query for rows linked to #408 still returns the now-unreviewed row, and if the next verdict is skipped the stale association persists.

raised.quote:
`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM enrich_failures
        WHERE issue_number = ? AND reviewed_at > ?`,
raised.claim: Saturation counts surviving review records rather than the post-creation attachments already posted to GitHub.
raised.why_it_breaks: An issue can receive 12 rows and become saturated, then a candidate-count transition clears one row's `reviewed_at` or a successful match deletes the failure row. The count drops to 11 and the issue accepts another attachment even though all 12 previous attachments remain on GitHub.

raised.claim: The timestamp comparison orders ISO strings rather than instants even though GitHub and the job use different precision.
raised.why_it_breaks: A review at `2026-08-14T10:00:00.500Z` is later than an issue created at `2026-08-14T10:00:00Z`, but SQLite sorts the review first because `.` sorts before `Z`. A genuine post-creation review in that second is omitted from the count.

raised.quote:
UPDATE enrich_failures
     SET issue_number = CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER)
   WHERE review_note LIKE '%→ #%'
     AND CAST(substr(review_note, instr(review_note, '→ #') + 3) AS INTEGER) > 0;
raised.claim: The migration promotes the first issue-like reference anywhere in the note to the authoritative link instead of identifying the legacy attachment suffix.
raised.why_it_breaks: For `compare → #120 before filing → #347`, it stores 120 instead of the appended issue 347. It also links a quiet review whose prose mentions an issue using that notation even though the job never attached the row.

raised.claim: Appending the scope after arbitrary-length prose can hide the routing constraint from the model while the planner still enforces it.
raised.why_it_breaks: The prompt only shows the first 2,000 characters of an open issue body. If the prose fills that budget, the model cannot see that the issue requires nonzero candidates and can repeatedly send it zero-candidate rows that the deterministic guard rejects.

raised.claim: The strict tool schema allows scope terms that the application schema rejects.
raised.why_it_breaks: For example, `col: 'candidates_count', op: 'contains', value: '0'` satisfies the tool schema but fails `ScopeTermSchema`. Because that schema is nested in `AnalysisSchema`, a single invalid proposal makes the whole payload fail validation rather than leaving its otherwise valid verdicts available.

raised.claim: The new scope check uses a snapshot that can be stale by the time the attachment is published and persisted.
raised.why_it_breaks: If enrichment changes a row from three candidates to zero during the awaited LLM call or GitHub writes, the captured row can still pass `candidates_count > 0`. The job then posts the attachment and updates the live failure by beer ID without checking whether the evidence changed.

raised.claim: The text and nullable dispatches still fall through to an existing comparison when a new operator is added.
raised.why_it_breaks: If a later schema change adds a text operator such as `starts_with` without updating this function, the numeric exhaustiveness check and final column-group check still pass. The new operator silently matches every nonempty string rather than checking its operand.
